Date: 2027-05-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Acme: Follow-up on performance SLOs & concurrency requirements

Marissa / Amy —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap from our side and the things we need to validate before we can finalize the pilot: 

- Latency targets: our product requires p50 <= 200ms for single-turn generation and p95 <= 800ms for streaming/longer responses (we need partial tokens served while model continues generating).
- Throughput: steady-state ~1,500 requests/sec during peak with average request size ~120 tokens.
- Concurrency: we expect up to 500 parallel requests hitting the same model in bursts. We also plan to use connection pooling from our side (keep-alive) and will open multiple persistent connections from our microservices.
- Streaming: we need chunked/streaming responses (server-sent events or chunked HTTP) for progressive rendering in the UI.

Two particular asks: can you confirm Redwood's default rate limits (requests/sec per project, concurrent request limits) and whether we should be on Dedicated capacity for this workload? Also: what does Redwood recommend for connection pooling and recommended client-side concurrency settings?

I'll share a short spike plan if we need to test capacity during the pilot.

Thanks,
John
VP of Product, Acme Corporation

Marissa / David —

Quick engineering take and proposal below. Assumptions: model is a 7B-family open model, average response ~120 tokens, average request ~30 tokens input. If the model is larger or token counts increase significantly, numbers will change.

Proposal summary (to send to Acme):
- Baseline hosted quotas (default): 1,000 req/sec per project, soft burst to 1,500 for short windows. Default concurrent request limit ~100.
- For Acme workload (steady 1,500 rps + bursts to 2,000 and concurrency ~500): recommend Dedicated pool or Hosted with elevated quotas on an Enterprise plan.

Recommended quota (pilot phase):
- Project-level requests/sec: 2,000 rps (sustained)
- Concurrency pool: 500 concurrent request slots total, implemented as a reserved pool with pre-warmed GPUs.
- Reserved high-priority pool: 200 slots guaranteed for production-critical traffic (to prevent noisy neighbors during bursts).
- Burst allowance: allow short bursts up to 3,000 rps using burst credits; average rate limits enforced per-minute windows.
- Token throughput: provision for ~180k tokens/sec to match average token sizes (we'll size GPU cluster accordingly).

Connection/Client guidance:
- Recommend 8-12 persistent connections per client process with keep-alive enabled (60s). Use connection pooling and HTTP/2 where possible. Avoid >50 concurrent connections from a single IP to reduce connection churn.
- Use streaming API for partial tokens; enable chunked responses and monitoring for stalled streams.

Operational notes:
- For guarantees on p95 under these patterns, Dedicated is the safer option. Hosted with elevated quotas can work for pilot but SLA/latency targets are best met on Dedicated.
- We'll provide a quota proposal PDF and a short pilot runbook.

Attaching the quota proposal and rough cost estimate.

Laura
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
